trades.thesis: TJX beat and raised on 11-18 (comps +4% vs plan 2-3%, FY comp now 4%, Marmaxx improved) and Target posted +5.6% comps on +5% traffic. US control retail sales came in at +0.6% vs 0.4%. Ross reports Q3 on 11-19 after the close with 8 straight EPS beats and comps of +7% and +10% in the last two quarters. It fell 4 days into the print and has lagged TJX's rebound. The edge is Ross's own print, since the sympathy gap is already in the fill price.

causal_chain.step: TJX Q3 FY27 (11-18 BMO): comps +4% vs 2-3% plan and 3.8% consensus, FY comp raised to 4%, Marmaxx improved. Target comps +5.6% on +5.0% traffic. Both show strong off-price and value traffic in the Aug-Oct quarter.

Ross competes for the same shopper as Marmaxx, and its quarter ended around Oct 31. Core retail sales beat (+0.6% vs 0.4%), so the same demand should show in Ross's Q3 comps. Ross has beaten EPS 8 of 8 quarters, with consensus EPS about $1.85 on $6.2B revenue.

ROST reports 11-19 after the close, and the reaction lands in my 3-day horizon. Weakest link: TJX's Marmaxx comp was only +2%, so strength may not transfer to Ross. The sympathy gap at today's open is already in my fill price.

sessions.feedback: Nothing blocked me this session. Two small things: read_page on prnewswire returned only navigation and no release body, so I had to rely on web_search snippets from the code tool. It would also help to know whether a stop that gaps through at the open fills at the open price or at the stop price. That decides whether closing manually into a gap beats letting the stop work.

Nothing blocked me, but two things would help.
1. The digest and news feed lag same-morning earnings. WSM, BABA and WMT prints were only in the news feed or web search, and I had to use web_search to find the WSM numbers. An earnings-results feed with EPS/revenue vs consensus and guidance for companies that reported pre-market would save calls.
2. scan shows pre-market only as a percent and a share count. An indication of whether the pre-market print is from IEX only or all venues would help me judge thin prints.

No blocking problems this session. Two things would have saved time. First, an earnings-consensus field (EPS and revenue expectations, and the typical post-earnings move) in scan, because I had to run web searches for it. Second, a sympathy-gap estimate: pre-market prints under 1,000 shares are too thin to judge the fill price for a read-through trade, and orders fill at the open, so I can't tell how much of the move I'll pay for. web_search is only reachable from inside code_execution and returns a JSON string, which costs extra calls. read_page on Benzinga still fails.

Digest 'biggest pre-market movers' ranks thin prints (100-600 shares) by sd, so most of the list is noise (e.g., KNX -8.5% on 396 shares). Filtering on minimum shares or a percent-of-average-day threshold would save budget. A tool returning the biggest losers and gainers of the previous session (not only gainers) would help find overreactions. A 'peers with earnings dates in the next 5 days' lookup by industry would suit the lagging-peer strategy.

Benzinga pages usually fail in read_page, though the digest links mostly point to Benzinga. Pre-market lists mix thin prints with real moves (e.g. NX -19% in the news roundup versus 0.0% in scan). Some prices look like spin-off artifacts (CTVA 9.43, -90% from 52-week high); a flag for corporate actions would help.

read_page fails on many major sites (CNBC, NBC, gurufocus), which makes the two-source requirement hard. The sandbox does not keep Python state between code_execution cells, so imports have to be repeated in every cell. A pre-market quote that shows volume (e.g. 828 shares) makes thin-volume REIT quotes misleading; a flag for low-volume pre-market prints would help.

The digest has no sector or industry-level sympathy view and the scan's industry labels are coarse (e.g. UBER/LYFT listed as 'Business Services'). Web search returns stale results for some queries. Earnings-call transcripts or a news-by-ticker endpoint would help.

summary:
Session 2026-11-20.

Session 2026-11-20. Closed ROST (bought 11-18 at 226.23, about -8% at the pre-market ~208). Q3 beat (comps +8%, EPS 1.91 vs 1.87, FY EPS raised) but Q4 comp guide only maintained at 4-5% and Q4 EPS cut 1c to 2.16-2.25 vs street 2.27, so the stock fell about 5% AH and pre-market; the thesis needed a forward raise and did not get one. Lesson recorded: retail reactions are driven by the next-quarter guide, not the FY raise.

Market: capitulation-style AI bust. SPY has had 6 straight down closes (-5.5% in 5d), SMH is -35% from its high, AMD -14% in 2 days, Taiex -6.2% on 11-20 (-17.5% in a week), KOSPI -5%. The 11-19 pre-market AI bounce fully reversed. ANT closed day one at 97.17 (+17%) and is -9.8% pre-market. Cash is beating SPY.

Looked at and rejected:
- ANT Nasdaq-100 fast entry (announcement Dec 11, entry Dec 21): the SpaceX precedent had no pre-inclusion run-up and fell 15% after joining, so no clean long.
- INTU read-through (Credit Karma guide cut, tighter lending) to TREE, NRDS, UPST, SOFI: weak chain, names already -50 to -67%, TREE costs 1% round trip.
- AI-capex chain (VRT, GEV, ORCL, DELL, FCX, EQIX, DLR): already -30 to -55%.
- Tankers and Hormuz: oil is flat.
- INSM (Sanofi takeover report), SNEX, LQDT, SVRA: first-order moves already priced.
- UNH (TD Cowen upgrade): CRUSH is still unresolved.

Next session: stay mostly cash unless the tape stabilises. Check whether Friday's gap-down held, and how the Michigan sentiment/inflation expectations and Fed speakers landed. Dates: HPE and ZM 11-23 AMC; BURL, BBY, DLTR 11-24 BMO; DELL 11-24 AMC. Look for an ANT fade setup after NDX inclusion in mid-Dec (check borrow), and watch neocloud shorts (CRWV, NBIS) on any bounce.

BUT SpaceX precedent (SPCX debut 6-12, joined NDX 7-7): no pre-inclusion run-up in the data, stock fell ~15% in 6 sessions after joining and -28% by Aug 5; "traders bought ahead and sold to the funds". So a long-ANT-into-inclusion trade is NOT a clean edge; a short after inclusion is the pattern but ANT likely hard to borrow.

- Retail: TJX beat/raise 11-18; TGT +5.6% comps; WMT beat/raise; WSM beat-no-raise sold -6-8%; ROST 11-19: beat (comps +8%, EPS 1.91 vs 1.87), FY EPS raised, Q4 comps kept 4-5% and Q4 EPS cut 1c to 2.16-2.25 vs street 2.27 -> -5.4% pre-market. GAP: warm weather softened Oct/early Nov, FY EPS 3.71-3.76, +3.5% pre. Next: BURL, BBY, DLTR 11-24 BMO; DELL 11-24 AMC; HPE, ZM 11-23 AMC.
- INTU 11-19 AMC: beat but cut FY27 revenue guide, all of it Credit Karma (growth 3-7% vs 11-13%), citing tighter lending conditions/consumer behaviour; Mailchimp sold to Bending Spoons $3.68B (vs $12B paid) ; stock -9.5% pre. Read-through to lead-gen/lender names (TREE, NRDS, UPST, AFRM, SOFI) is plausible but weak: TREE (+32% on 11-04 Q3) and NRDS (rev +11%) reported fine, consumer-finance names are already -50% to -67% from highs, and Intuit also blamed Credit Karma Tax launch and revenue-timing changes. Not traded (TREE shortable but $0.5B cap, 0.5% slippage, 8% daily vol).
- Trades so far: PUBM (11-06 long 4%, closed 11-13 +12.5%, +9.9 pts vs SPY). ROST (11-18 long 4% at 226.23, closed 11-20 around 208 pre-market, about -8%, loses to SPY by a wide margin). Sessions with no new trade: 10-29, 11-04, 11-16, 11-17, 11-19, 11-20.
- LESSONS:
 1) Peer-earnings-lag longs: PUBM worked (dated catalyst, peer lagged) but ROST failed (11-18 buy -> 11-20 print). Retail print reactions are driven by the NEXT quarter guide (holiday Q4), not the FY raise (which is arithmetic after a Q3 beat). WSM on 11-19 already showed beat-without-raise sells; I should have treated ROST's Q4 guide risk as the main risk and sized/avoided it. Avoid buying into a print where the market's whisper needs a raise of forward guide after a 4-day run-down in a falling tape.
 2) By the pre-open session, first-order and obvious second-order moves are priced (GDS -14.7% a day before I looked; cyber peers +4-6% pre-market on PANW). The sympathy gap is in the fill price.
 3) Regulatory proposals (CRUSH) and big-cap drops can stay down for months: need a catalyst, not just a big drop (UNH Jan-2026 analog).
 4) In capitulation tapes (SPY 6 down days, Asia -5%), pre-open 'bounce' longs have a ~coin-flip edge at best; cash is the position. Wait for a stabilisation signal (e.g., VIX peak, index holding a gap-down) rather than catching a 6-day fall.
- Open ideas: ANT after NDX inclusion (Dec 18-21) as a fade, if borrowable; NDX funds sell other mega-caps to fund ANT buying (check QQQ-heavy names mid-Dec); tower churn (AMT/CCI/SBAC); JBS/China beef quotas; neocloud shorts after bounces fade (CRWV/NBIS -5% pre-market 11-20 again, trend is down); MA-exposed clinic landlords/brokers; BURL into 11-24 print (warm weather hit Gap/outerwear in Oct-Nov); consumer-lending lead-gen (TREE) if more lender-pullback evidence.

prompt:
Your universe is every eligible US stock. Your style is weird, second-order research.

Everyone else reads the headline and trades the company in it. You trade the company the headline
does not mention. Start from events in the news and follow the consequences outward: suppliers,
customers, competitors, substitutes, regions, commodities, logistics, weather, regulation, the
odd dependency nobody has priced. A storm hits the region that grows potatoes for a fast-food chain;
which other chain gains, which frozen-food maker loses, which railroad hauls the replacement crop?

- Every new position, long or short, needs a causal chain of at least two steps from the event to
  the company you trade, each step with a source where possible. Code rejects a trade whose ticker
  or company name appears in today's digest headlines, so the link has to be one you found. The
  losers at the end of a chain are as fair game as the winners: short them.
- Borderline delusional is the brief, but the chain still has to be real: each step should be
  something you could defend with evidence. Write down the step most likely to be wrong.
- Spreading across several smaller bets suits this style better than one big one. Small companies
  cost more to trade, so make the expected move worth it.
- Use search_symbols to find the companies at the end of a chain. Read their exposure, do not assume it.
